subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should literal `openai` session route state be owned for doctor cleanup by a new OpenAI provider owner, by the existing Codex doctor owner, or by provider-agnostic stale-auto-fallback repair?
rationale: Source proves the owner registry gap, but OpenClaw policy treats canonical `openai` as both the OpenAI provider id and the default Codex app-server route for OpenAI agent models, so automation should not choose the permanent ownership boundary alone.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an OpenAI route-state doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and tests for stale auto fallback cleanup without expanding Codex legacy ownership.

options.title: Codex owns OpenAI app-server state
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers want OpenAI agent-model route state treated as Codex-owned for repair.

options.title: Make stale auto fallback repair generic
options.body: Repair `modelOverrideSource: "auto"` overrides outside the configured route without relying on provider-owner metadata for canonical providers.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI route-state doctor owner for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and tests for stale auto fallback cleanup without expanding Codex legacy ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged doctor/Codex route-state repair PRs make this the clearest available owner-boundary decision signal.
